description: What an OWNER'S RIGHTS stored procedure may not create, measured cell by cell on a real account, because the documented sentence ('cannot create named temporary objects') is both narrower and wider than it sounds. Every spelling of a temporary TABLE - TEMPORARY, TEMP, LOCAL TEMPORARY, GLOBAL TEMPORARY, VOLATILE, IF NOT EXISTS, OR REPLACE, and the CTAS form - is refused as the SAME kind, because live folds them all to 'temporary TABLE'. STAGE and FILE FORMAT name their own kinds, and so now do VIEW and FUNCTION, which used to escape this guard entirely: before the grammar learned their temporary spellings both failed as unsupported SYNTAX long before the owner's-rights check ran, so the refusal they were supposed to produce could not be asserted at all. TRANSIENT is NOT temporary and is created without complaint, as is a permanent table. EXECUTE AS CALLER is unrestricted. And the restriction belongs to the HANDLER LANGUAGES: a LANGUAGE SQL procedure creates a temporary table under owner's rights on a real account, so frostlake must not refuse it - and the rule follows the STATEMENT rather than the call tree, so a Java owner's-rights handler that CALLs a SQL procedure creating a temporary table is allowed, because that statement never passes through the handler's session. Converted 1:1 from scripting/OwnersRightsTemporaryObjectTest (now retired). Two notes the Java carried and this suite keeps: the .collect() is not decoration, because Snowpark's session.sql is LAZY on live so without an action the statement is never submitted and the refusal never fires; and PACKAGES is what puts Snowpark on the compiler's classpath live, though frostlake supplies its own stub either way. The Java looked at the ROOT cause message; frostlake raises the sentence at the top level, while live wraps it in a Java stack trace - the two agree on the claim and differ only in the packaging, which is why messageContains is the right shape here.
